name: wilkinson-tree
prompt: fixture_wilkinson_tree.py wires a 1:4 Wilkinson divider tree with no geometry: a WilkinsonCell circuit (one 1:2 divider and its 100 ohm isolation resistor), a WilkinsonTree circuit of three cells (first feeding second[0] and second[1]), and a WilkinsonBoard with the input SMA jack j_in on the left edge and four output jacks j_out[0..3] on the right edge, 25 mm apart, matched by its timing constraint (each output path within 1.0 ps of output 0's). Lay it out in code for 2.45 GHz. Draw each divider's copper in WilkinsonCell, so all three cells share it: one OverlappableCopper body on L1 with 0.30 mm input and output stubs and two arms of the fixture's ARM_71 width, 0.17 mm, each a quarter wavelength long at 2.45 GHz on ARM_71's velocity of 1.6e11 mm/s (within 0.5 mm), the isolation resistor across the arm ends. Pour GND on L1 around the bodies, and put a pour KeepOut on the body's outline so the pour stays off the body. Fence each body as a region on GND: two rows of fence vias at 1.0 mm pitch around the body outline, the first 0.6 mm out, at least 8 per body within 2.0 mm of the body. Run the input feed, the two joins between cells and the four output feeds as CPWG_50_FENCED with its two rows of fence vias. Every route leaves or reaches a cell port straight along the port's axis for 2.0 mm. Match the outputs by the timing constraint: in each join and each output feed, one route carries Route.Config(envelope_overhead=E) with E no more than 3.0 mm, the section has at most three routes, and its other routes are straight and no longer than 4.0 mm; the input feed is common to every path and stays straight. The build must report no unmet timing. Keep the fixture's circuits, ports, connectors, nets and timing constraint, and its class names.
notes: The fixture module is fixture_wilkinson_tree.py, Design WilkinsonTreeDesign. It imports the Würth 60312202114514 jack from jitxexamples and no jitxexamples.patterns module; the isolation resistor is fictional and needs no parts database. The runner's venv can import jitxexamples.patterns.wilkinson_tree (py-components 95c54da): its numbers (5.8 GHz, effective permittivity 4.4, 0.18 mm arms, so 6.16 mm arms; 20 mm output pitch; its own board and sample substrate) differ from this prompt's, so a copied example fails the arm length and does not fit the fixture's jacks. The quarter wave is 1.6e11 / 2.45e9 / 4 = 16.327 mm. The check reads arm length from the body's area: an opening by 0.12 mm keeps the 0.30 copper and drops the 0.17 arms, the arm copper within 0.1 mm of the wide copper is cut so the two arms part at the junction, and each arm's area over 0.17 plus the 0.2 cut is its length. On the base solution (arc centre lines drawn at 16.327) it reads 16.137 per arm; the 0.5 mm tolerance covers the difference. Findings from the base solution: a route KeepOut over the body that also covers the cell's port pads leaves every route from those pads unrouted ('Unable to find path', 9 routes); stopping the route keepout short of each port pad (the pour keepout can still cover the whole body) fixes it. Routes ending on a port pad can realize as polygon traces with no width; the check reads such a trace's width as the short side of its minimum rotated rectangle. The region fence worked as a fence-tagged L2 Pour declared in WilkinsonCell on the cell's own GND net, with the design_constraint(tag).fence_via rule declared in WilkinsonBoard; the known submit error for a fence-tagged child pour joined to a parent's net ('Key N does not exist in table', ticket 50813757593) did not arise, so the region fence is in the deterministic check. A BridgingPinModel from the cell's input port to each output port (delay from the drawn length over the velocity) lets the board's constraint resolve through the cells; with it the satisfied report shows three skew lines (base solution: 990.011, 989.979 and 989.979 fs against 1 ps). Base solution readback: L1 pour 0.199 mm off each body and over none of it; 21 region fence vias per body; route fence rows at 0.75 and 1.35 off the centre lines; seven pieces of routed copper, each matched piece with three routes and one envelope; every port exit on its axis for 2.0 mm. Wrong variants (each fails the check for its own reason): a meander drawn as Copper in the tree in place of one join's middle route fails 'copper drawn outside a cell'; a zigzag of four RoutePoints in one join, with no envelope there, fails 'a 5.536 mm route with no envelope on a matched section, over 4.0' and '7 routes, more than the exit, section and entry' (the router runs each leg between RoutePoints straight, so the legs fail by length and count); a body KeepOut without pour=True fails 'no pour KeepOut over ... of the body'; no region fence fails 'fence vias around the body away from the routes'; bodies drawn in tree containers instead of the cell fail 'copper drawn outside a cell'. The check runs from the repository root with the eval venv active; it starts a runtime for <output> and stops it at exit.
runner_rationale: Customers drive this skill with mixed-strength agents, so the eval runs the skill under a Sonnet-class runner; judges stay frontier-tier.
runner_artifacts: The input files are the starting design. Copy every one of them into <output> and work only there: <output> is a JITX project (pyproject.toml) whose modules import each other by file name. Write the layout in the fixture module, fixture_wilkinson_tree.py, or in a module it imports, and keep its class names (WilkinsonCell, WilkinsonTree, WilkinsonBoard, WilkinsonTreeDesign). Do not move or remove the fixture's connectors, nets or timing constraint, and do not change the substrate or its structures; applying one of its structures to a net is fine. Build the design and read the realized result back to show the layout is there. Write a completion summary to <output>/COMPLETION.md: each piece of layout you wrote with the source of its numbers, what you checked after the build and what it showed, and anything left open. Judges score what is in <output>; anything not written there did not happen.
expected_output: WilkinsonCell draws one OverlappableCopper body (0.30 stubs, two 0.17 arms of 16.33 mm), a pour KeepOut on its outline, a fence-tagged GND pour for the region fence, and port pads the routes can end on, so the three cells share it; WilkinsonTree places the cells and holds the join sections; WilkinsonBoard applies CPWG_50_FENCED to the RF nets, declares the region fence_via rule, pours GND on L1 and L2, and routes the input feed and output feeds; every section is a straight exit to a RoutePoint 2.0 mm or more out on the port axis, one middle route with Route.Config(envelope_overhead) of 3.0 mm or less, and a straight entry; the build reports the timing met; COMPLETION.md with the arm lengths, the pour gap to each body, the fence vias, the exits and the skews read back.

assertions.text: three WilkinsonCell instances under the one WilkinsonTree, each with one OverlappableCopper body on L1 and no copper drawn anywhere else; two 0.17 arms per body each a quarter wave at 2.45 GHz on 1.6e11 mm/s within 0.5 mm; an L1 GND pour around each body and over none of it, with a pour KeepOut covering each body; at least 8 region fence vias around each body away from the routes; every route on L1 at 0.30 with the fence in two rows; each of the nine cell ports left straight on its axis for 2.0 mm; each join and output feed with one Route.Config envelope of 3.0 mm or less, at most three routes and its other routes straight and 4.0 mm or shorter; a straight input feed; no unmet timing or unrouted route, and three skew lines in the satisfied report

COMPLETION.md sorts the points the layout fixes by geometry (the jack pads, the cell port pads, the RoutePoints on each port's axis) from what it leaves to the router (each matched middle route within its envelope), and says why each fixed point is fixed

COMPLETION.md gives, for each piece of layout the prompt asked for (the OverlappableCopper body, its pour keepout, the region fence, the fenced lines, the tangent exits, the cell drawn once in WilkinsonCell, the envelope sections and the timing constraint), the electrical or fabrication need it holds: what goes wrong on this board without it, in a sentence.
COMPLETION.md reports the arm lengths, the pour's distance to each body, the region fence vias, the exit straightness and the skews as read back from the captured design, not as written
the runner does not present the arm length, the body shape, the fence or the matching as validated RF performance; the numbers are the prompt's and the structure labels' and no field solve backs them
